page.text:
The formal fraction-pair construction realizes a rational number as an
equivalence class $[(a, b)]_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of integer pairs $(a, b) \in \mathbb{Z} \times (\mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\})$.
The familiar fraction notation $a/b$ designates this entire equivalence class
rather than a specific pair of integers.

A critical obligation of this quotient construction is verifying
*well-definedness*: if $(a, b) \sim (a', b')$ and $(c, d) \sim (c', d')$,
then the defined addition and multiplication must produce equivalent outputs:
$$ (ad + cb, bd) \sim (a'd' + c'b', b'd') \quad \text{and} \quad (ac, bd) \sim (a'c', b'd'). $$
Similarly, the ordering condition must be independent of chosen representatives.
The map $\iota : \mathbb{Z} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{Q}$ defined by $\iota(n) = [(n, 1)]_{\mathbb{Q}}$
is an injective ring homomorphism, allowing us to identify $\mathbb{Z}$ canonically
as an ordered subring of $\mathbb{Q}$.
